title: Epochal Promote Controller with Health-Decider Epochs and Deterministic Rollback Plan
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce Epochal Promote Controller to enable deterministic, epoch-driven staged rollouts with configurable health deciders and snapshot rollback. No public API surface changes; ops-only feature behind feature flag.
description: Summary: Adds a new 'Epochal Promote Controller' that coordinates multi-stage model promotions by driving progress in discrete epochs (time-bounded windows). Each epoch evaluates a configurable set of health deciders (latency SLOs, error-rate guards, quality regressions from eval hooks, and production signal fusion) and either advances, holds, or triggers a deterministic rollback. Motivation: previous progressive-swap controllers reacted to continuous signals which made reproducing and debugging rollouts difficult and led to non-deterministic rollbacks; this work makes rollouts replayable and auditable by snapshotting state at epoch boundaries and applying deterministic decision logic. Design notes: controller defines epochs as units of observation; at epoch end it computes a signed health vector via decider plugins, writes an immutable epoch snapshot into rollout journal, and uses a deterministic decision graph to choose promote/hold/rollback. Snapshots are compressed and stored in rollout-snapshots S3 bucket for later replay and dry-run. Safety: automatic rollback plan is deterministic and accompanied by an admin-friendly playbook; manual hold and forced-promote ops are still supported. Includes integration with A/B splitter: the controller can treat A/B experiments as first-class epochs allowing metric fusion across cohorts and a final promotion decision only when cohort-level deciders pass. Shadow traffic handling: adds a shadow-drain phase that validates production shadows against live responses while preserving request idempotency and request traceability for debugging. Migration path: gated behind rollout.feature.epochal_promote boolean flag; existing rollout controllers remain unchanged. Checklist: - [x] core controller implementation and CRD - [x] decider plugin interface and three built-in deciders (latency, errors, quality-regression) - [x] snapshot journal writer/reader with compression - [x] dry-run replay CLI and e2e tests - [x] console UI: epoch timeline visualization and manual rollback button - [x] migration feature flag and operator docs - [x] runbook for on-call. How to test locally: run tests/integration/epochal_promote_test.go which spins a minimal orchestrator and a two-epoch plan; run 'rdw rollout replay --snapshot <id>' to reproduce a historical decision. Related work: builds on ENG-4821 (deterministic rollbacks), ENG-4950 (shadow validation harness).
commit_summary: 1) add CRD and controller scaffolding; 2) implement epoch state machine and snapshot journal; 3) add decider interface and three deciders; 4) implement shadow-drain step and A/B fusion hook; 5) console UI timeline and playback; 6) integration tests and runbook updates.
review_comments: Evan Zhang: Can we keep epoch snapshots compact? Consider delta-compression between consecutive epochs. Author: implemented gzip+delta index and added size metrics to journal.
Priya Menon: How does this interact with existing canary hooks? Author: the controller will call existing hooks at epoch boundaries; compatibility layer added in decider adapter.
Liam O'Connor: CI flagged flaky integration test on first run. Author: increased test timeouts and added deterministic seeding; re-ran CI and all tests passed.
merge_outcome_note: Merged after approvals. Feature gated; rollout controller enabled in staging cluster for 48h soak, then promoted to prod-nightly job for further validation. No incidents during staged run.
